paper.title: A contribution to the mathematical theory of epidemics

headline: SIR threshold (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; attack(R0=0.8)=0.0061, attack(R0=2.0)=0.7952 (analytic 0.7968)

verdicts.gate: P1 epidemic threshold at R0=1 (attack<0.05 at R0=0.8 AND >0.30 at R0=2.0)
P2 final size at R0=2.0 within +/-10% of analytic ln(S0/Sinf)=R0(1-Sinf/N)
P3 attack rate monotone non-decreasing in R0; <0.05 at R0=0.8

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model (well-mixed mass-action SIR); no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the epidemic threshold + final-size result and would catch an artifact

citations: Kermack, W.O. & McKendrick, A.G. (1927). A contribution to the mathematical theory of epidemics. Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 115(772):700-721. doi:10.1098/rspa.1927.0118.
Brauer, F. (2008). Compartmental models in epidemiology. In Mathematical Epidemiology, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1945, pp. 19-79. Springer. (final-size relation ln(S0/Sinf)=R0(1-Sinf/N)).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction validated against the analytic final-size relation
